analysis:
Only scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py is in this batch, and only its BASE text and a truncated patch excerpt were supplied. It is an offline unittest that parses .github/workflows/ci.yml and the composite action, and it ships no runtime product code. The patch visibly adds helper constants and functions (CHECKOUT/CACHE pins, SAVE_POLICY, VALIDATE_GIT, SPARSE_PATTERNS, GIT_CACHE_STEPS, uses(), checkout_options(), work_steps()). The helpers imply the PR also changes ci.yml. It apparently adds a shared .git cache, sparse checkout and a SAVE_CACHES policy where only pushes to master or dev save caches. Test changes at the head side include lines 792-923 and 969-997, which are not in the supplied head text.

The base text shows existing guards that the test enforces: pinned action SHAs, fail-closed fixture steps, no continue-on-error, no secrets or backend references in the provider job, and save-on-miss rules for pull requests. The visible patch does not weaken any of them. The patch excerpt is truncated, so I could not confirm whether the new tests keep the existing pinned-SHA, no-secrets and PR-no-save assertions.

No canonical threat IDs apply directly. The test only touches CI hygiene around the TB-003/TB-007 artifact, and release signing and qualification (A-017, T-054) are outside this file. Remaining questions for integration: (1) does the ci.yml change restore a .git cache only for trusted refs, and does it use the VALIDATE_GIT fsck check before use? (2) Can pull requests from forks poison caches that master or dev pushes later restore? (3) Does the cache key prevent cross-branch poisoning of the .git or build caches used by release lanes? None of these is verifiable from the supplied evidence, so I record them as unverified and not as findings.
